title: Create and Identify Products
readerIntent: Create a product and variants with stable identity.
priorKnowledge: Know catalog, type, attributes, units, categories, and lifecycle.
summary: Create stable product identity first, then variants and relationships; prices and stock reference that identity but remain separately owned.

sections.heading: Steps
items: Select tenant, enterprise, staged catalog, product type, and stable code.
Add names, descriptions, categories, classifications, attributes, units, media references, and lifecycle.
Define variant dimensions and stable variant codes without embedding price or balance.
Validate required data and relationships, start approval workflow, and publish the approved version.
Verify Online product, search projection, cache refresh, and unresolved Price/Stock behavior.

sections.heading: Product and variant identity
paragraphs: A Product represents a sellable concept or family; a Variant represents a stable choice such as size, color, storage, packaging, or another dimension. Codes remain stable across staged and online systems.
Price and stock reference product or variant identity but remain owned by Pricing and Inventory.

sections.heading: Product type flexibility
items: Physical goods measured by pieces, mass, volume, or area.
Digital or service products with no physical stock.
Real-estate land using area and location attributes.
Agricultural land, crops, or bulk produce using appropriate Units.
Bundles, configurable products, and project-defined classifications.
Each type enables only relevant attributes and lifecycle behavior.

sections.heading: Catalog and relationships
paragraphs: Products belong to a staged product catalog when governed authoring and publishing are enabled. Categories, classifications, media, Units, Sites, Stores, and related products use their owning contracts.
A relationship never copies a price, balance, content page, or provider record into Product authority.

sections.heading: Example: phone variants
paragraphs: Create iPhone 17 Pro Max as a product family with stable variants for storage and color. Pricing assigns eligible price rows by enterprise, Store, Site, country, currency, segment, and group. Inventory records stock by variant and source.
Publishing deploys the approved online product. A zone can remain unsellable even when another zone has stock.

sections.heading: Validation and lifecycle
items: Unique stable code and valid variant dimensions.
Required type-specific attributes and compatible Units.
No cyclic or incompatible relationships.
Draft, review, approved, published, discontinued, and archived behavior.
Dependency validation before publish.
Migration when identity or variant structure changes.

sections.heading: Complete guide: How To Create And Identify Products
paragraphs: Product gives an enterprise a dependable identity for anything it offers or manages. The same foundation can represent a product family, a sellable SKU, a service, a unique asset such as a land parcel, or a future bundle.

sections.heading: Add related products, bundles, packaging, and media
paragraphs: Use Product-owned associations when the relationship is part of the Product graph. Relations describe accessories, compatibility, replacements, substitutes, cross-sells, up-sells, and related Items. Bundle Entries add ordered components with exact quantities and Units-owned Unit codes. Packaging records contained quantity, dimensions, and weight with exact decimal strings and existing Units.

Use Product Media References when a Product needs a primary image, thumbnail, gallery image, swatch, zoom image, video, manual, or datasheet. Product stores the Product-owned role, order, locale, alt text, and exactly one `nMedia` reference: either `mediaCode` for one concrete file or `mediaSetCode` for a reusable set of variants. Upload, generated URLs, provider keys, MIME policy, checksums, and binary storage remain outside Product.
Nodics rejects self-links, duplicates, configured graph cycles, media assignments that point to both or neither `mediaCode` and `mediaSetCode`, incomplete measurements, and unknown Units or Items.
items: Create or select the Product Item that owns the association.
For related products, choose the configured relation type and target Item.
For bundles, provide exact component quantity and Unit.
For packaging, provide paired measurement values and Units.
For media, upload or select the asset through Media Management first, then save the Product media assignment using `mediaCode` or `mediaSetCode`.

sections.heading: Read Products Online
paragraphs: An authenticated customer application supplies Catalog, Item type, Item code, optional locale, and only the expansions it needs. Product reads the active Online release and can include identifiers, categories, attributes, classifications, variants, relations, bundles, packaging, and media.

The response includes the active release version. If that pointer changes, the next cache key changes automatically. Product uses the configured nCache channel, so an operator may select NodeCache, Redis, or Hazelcast without changing Product code. Only one provider should serve the logical channel at a time.

Product search documents are sent through nSearch after activation. Search and cache are projections: if either fails, the verified Product release remains authoritative and Online. A durable projection job records the failure so an operator can retry incomplete work.

sections.heading: Diagnose Online publication
paragraphs: An authorized operator can view the active and previous release, pointer revision, manifest hash and record count, deployment receipts, correlation ID, and cache/search projection status. When a projection is incomplete, the operator can run bounded reconciliation. Do not republish, edit Online records, or change the active pointer merely to repair search or cache.

sections.heading: Correct or retire information
paragraphs: Names, descriptions, flags, and other permitted fields can be corrected through the update intent. Enterprise, Catalog ownership, Item type, Item code, and Identifier identity cannot be changed through an ordinary update.
Retire obsolete records instead of deleting them. This preserves historical references from Pricing, Inventory, orders, and integrations.
